text: Convert the following EER model in to the relational model. Indicate the primary keys and the foreign keys of the resulted relations clearly.
Consider a relation R (A, B, C, D, E) with the following set of functional dependencies over R: F={B->D,D>E,AB~>C,B~>E}

subquestions.label: a)
subquestions.text: Find all the keys that follow from the given FDs using attribute closure.

subquestions.label: b)
subquestions.text: Is R in 3NF? Give reasons for your conclusion.

subquestions.label: c)
subquestions.text: Is R in BCNF? Give reasons for your conclusion. If R is not in BCNF, convert it to a set of BCNF relations.

text: Consider the following relations in a Movie Database.

subquestions.label: a)
subquestions.text: Use SQL queries to answer following questions.

subquestions.label: i.
subquestions.text: Display names of all the Actors in the movie 'The Princess Bride'.

subquestions.label: ii.
subquestions.text: Display all directors who directed 500 movies or more, in descending order of the number of movies they directed. List the directors' names and the number of movies each of them directed.

subquestions.label: b)
subquestions.text: Create a view named movieDirection that contains movie title, movie genre type, year, director's first name, last name and actors for those movies.

subquestions.label: c)
subquestions.text: Create a function named as getActorCount, which takes movie title as the input and returns the number of actors that acted in that particular movie.

subquestions.label: d)
subquestions.text: Assume that rank of the Movie are based on the number of stars the reviewers have rewarded. Write a trigger to update the rank when the reviewer places stars in a new movie.
